extracted.intended_audience: young physician-scientists (and their institutions/mentors) applying for the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applicants (physician-scientists) and their institutions to apply for the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award, including eligibility, selection criteria, required commitments, funding terms, and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Clinical Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical research is defined as: (a) Patient-oriented research: research conducted with human subjects (or on material of human origin such as tissues, specimens and cognitive phenomena) including patient‑based studies of mechanisms of human disease, diagnostic and therapeutic interventions, clinical trials and development of new technologies for detection, treatment and prevention of human cancers; (b) Epidemiologic and behavioral studies; (c) Outcomes research and health services research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must be involved in patient care and be conducting research that has the potential to be translated to impact patients. The proposal must adhere to this definition of clinical research as a condition of eligibility and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handshake Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference is given to research that adheres to the 'Handshake Rule,' meaning that the physician will conduct research studies that directly involve patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handshake Rule does not apply to pathologist candidates. Adherence is a specific selection consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Research Effort – 80% Protected Time
rubrics_metrics.description: During each award year, the applicant must commit a minimum of 80% of their full-time professional effort to the conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare circumstances the CIA Committee may consider a very modest reduction from 80% if the Department Chair provides a compelling justification, states the guaranteed percentage of effort, and describes safeguards to protect the applicant's research. Applicants must document protected time as part of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor Role and Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mentor must foster the applicant’s development of knowledge, technical and analytical skills, and capacity for scientific inquiry in human disease‑oriented clinical and translational research, and act as an advocate for the applicant at departmental, institutional, and professional levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor commitment and quality are assessed during selection. No more than two Damon Runyon Clinical Investigators may be funded to work with the same Mentor at any given time (including co‑mentors). Only one application will be accepted from a Mentor per review session (including co‑mentors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Criterion – Excellence of Applicant and Mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated on the excellence of the applicant and the Mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excellence includes past productivity, qualifications, and evidence that the applicant and Mentor are positioned to succeed in clinical/translational cancer research; CIAC places a premium on innovation and creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Criterion – Innovation, Creativity, Quality and Originality of Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The research proposal must demonstrate innovation, creativity, quality, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIAC emphasizes novelty and creative approaches in disease‑oriented clinical research when scoring and selecting awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Criterion – Commitment of Mentor and Institution to Trainee Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment of the Mentor and institution to the development and training of the applicant as an independent clinical, translational, or outcomes‑based investigator is a selection criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for evidence of institutional support such as comprehensive start‑up packages, ample laboratory space, and protected research time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Criterion – Applicant's Commitment to Clinical/Translational/Cancer Prevention Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of the applicant’s commitment to clinical translational and/or cancer prevention research and their ability to apply laboratory advances to clinical problems is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate past and planned activities that show sustained commitment and translation from bench to bedside or prevention-focused work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection Criterion – Importance to the Field
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the proposed research to the field of cancer and/or cancer prevention is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should articulate significance, potential impact on cancer medicine, and relevance to clinical practice or prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Clinical Research Definition as Review Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence of the proposal to the Foundation’s definition of clinical research (see page) is a specific basis for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure project clearly fits within defined categories (patient‑oriented, epidemiologic/behavioral, or outcomes/health services research) and involves patient‑impact potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility – Institutional Nomination and Invited Institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must be nominated by their institution; applications will only be accepted from institutions invited to submit by the Foundation. Three nominations per institution (including affiliated schools) will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your institution is on the invited list and coordinate nominations centrally; institutional nomination is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility – Position, Degrees, and Licensure
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must hold an independent Assistant Professor position (or equivalent) at a U.S. institution, have received an MD, DO, or MD/PhD from an accredited institution, completed subspecialty training, be U.S. Board eligible, and hold a valid, active U.S. medical license at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor, adjunct, or acting positions are not eligible. The applicant must apply within the first four years of Assistant Professor (cut‑off date indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility – Appointment Time Window
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must apply within the first four (4) years of their Assistant Professor or equivalent full‑time faculty appointment (Cut‑off date: July 1, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may apply up to two times during this eligibility period; verify appointment start date against cut‑off rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility – R01/Equivalent Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates holding or awarded R01s (or R01‑equivalent grants such as the DP2 and DP5) at the time of application are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current funding status before applying; the award targets early independent investigators without major independent federal R01‑level support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Procedural Requirements and Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via Altum | Proposal Central (search Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award). Applications are due by 4:00 pm Eastern Time on January 20, 2026. Application instructions and forms are provided on the Foundation's application guidelines and within Proposal Central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Proposal Central forms and Damon Runyon Application Guidelines precisely; institutional nomination and proper forms are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Terms and Allowable Uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is $600,000 over three years ($200,000 per year) to the awardee’s institution. Funds are flexible and may be used for the Investigator’s stipend and/or fringe benefits (up to $130,000 annually), salaries for professional and technical personnel, special equipment, supplies, and other miscellaneous items required to conduct the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No part of the grant may be used for indirect costs or institutional overhead; adhere to listed allowable categories and investigator salary caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Funding and Overlap Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may receive funding from other sources, but no other private-source physician‑scientist mentored career development award may be held concurrently with the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award. Federal physician‑scientist career development awards (e.g., K08, K12, K23) are allowed. Scientific or budgetary overlap with other funded projects is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All current and pending support must be reported and the relationship to the Damon Runyon‑funded project explained; contact the Foundation for questions about concurrent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt Repayment Program Eligibility and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will retire up to $100,000 of qualifying medical school debt for awardees (paid over the award period, not to exceed $33,333 in any one year), provided candidates first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program and meet documentation and other conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying loans: tuition and direct educational expenses and interest; loans for living expenses do not qualify. Documentation (receipts, agreements, payment info) must be submitted within one month of acceptance and annually. Consolidated loans require underlying loan agreements. Loan repayments stop during leaves without pay unless the Foundation grants written permission. Participants must disclose other debt relief programs. The Foundation may require repayment of amounts if the award is terminated early unless the participant continues in clinical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax Liability Reimbursement for Loan Payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Loan repayments are taxable income; the Foundation will approximate the added tax liability and pay an 'Additional Tax Payment' to offset increased Federal, State, and Local taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assumed tax rate will be determined by the Foundation in its sole discretion and may not equal the participant’s actual tax rate; payments will be reported to the IRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Presentations Acknowledgment Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications (including abstracts) resulting from Foundation‑supported projects must carry the acknowledgment: '[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator supported (in part) by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (CI‑#[___]).' Awardees should identify themselves as Damon Runyon Clinical Investigators when presenting work or accepting honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download and use the Foundation logo as provided for posters and presentations; proper acknowledgment is a condition of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers, Termination and Institutional Approval Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Clinical Investigator wishes to discontinue the project, leave the designated institution, or modify any award agreement, they must seek approval from the Foundation in advance. Failure to obtain approval will result in immediate termination and may jeopardize future awards to the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to the sponsoring institution; changes must be negotiated with the Foundation prior to action to avoid termination and payback obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Award Statement and Invention Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All awardees must adhere to the Foundation's award statement and invention policy. The Foundation will not modify the terms of its policies at the request of individual institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies are Board‑approved and non‑negotiable; review award statement and invention policy carefully before accepting the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Review and Continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is granted for three years and is subject to review and approval each year as set out under the terms and conditions. A Continuation Grant exists to provide up to two additional years of support for awardees approaching the end of their awards who need extra time/funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation support is intended to complete promising research or initiate/continue a clinical trial; continuation requires submission of required forms and adherence to reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and Forms for Awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit required forms: Award Statement, Award Acceptance Form, Loan Repayment Form, Budget Form, Expenditure Report Form, Intellectual Property Disclosure Form, Annual Progress Report Form, Final Progress Report Form, Questionnaire, and Continuation Grant documents when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and accurate submission of forms and progress reports is a condition of award renewal and loan repayment eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at Annual Symposium
rubrics_metrics.description: All current Clinical Investigators are expected to attend the annual Accelerating Cancer Cures Annual Symposium to highlight achievements and promote interactions with sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symposium participation is an expectation of awardees and part of program engagement with industry sponsors.
